title: What The Taiko Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 108bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Japanese philosophy absurdist thunder
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The taiko drum is not a subtle instrument
It is a barrel the size of a small car with intent
You don't tap a taiko — you address it from the shoulder
Every note a statement and the statement gets no older

[Pre-Chorus]
I watched a taiko ensemble once and stood in the back
Because standing at the front felt like standing on a track

[Chorus]
What does the taiko know that I don't know?
It knows that some truths need to land with the force of a blow
What does the taiko know in an open field?
It knows that thunder was the original percussion revealed
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The taiko drummer's stance is called the kamae — a commitment
You plant your feet and raise your arms with full submission
The bachi sticks are not held loosely, they are held with purpose
Every strike an intention rising up from under surface

[Bridge]
Buddhist temples used it, samurai deployed it too
Festivals and funerals and everything in between asked too
The taiko doesn't whisper and the taiko doesn't hint
The taiko makes its position clear without the slightest squint

[Outro]
Taiko knows… the body is the message… taiko knows
That's my boy
